Search cyclic two-frequency orbit codes then break symmetry with LP polishing and basin-hopping.
direction: Search for a symmetric orbit configuration, then break the symmetry: parameterize configurations invariant under rotations acting as $R(a\theta)$ on coordinates $(x_1,x_2)$, $R(b\theta)$ on $(x_3,x_4)$, and trivially on $x_5$, for small integer pairs $(a,b)$ such as $(1,2),(1,3),(2,3)$, with several seed orbits (generic orbits of size equal to the group order, plus points in coordinate planes or on the $x_5$-axis) whose sizes sum to 173. Optimize only the few orbit representatives, the rotation step, and relative phases with a smooth-max objective, then LP-polish in the symmetry-reduced space; afterwards release all 173 points and polish without symmetry constraints, using the symmetric optimum as a genuinely different starting basin. Also try nearby orbit-size decompositions differing by moving one orbit to fixed/plane points, because an orbit code automatically has balanced contact degrees and no rattler, and even if symmetry is suboptimal, symmetry-breaking from it explores topology unreachable by perturbing the record.

idea: Non-greedy population basin-hopping with contact-graph diversity and Procrustes-aligned recombination to find an equilibrated topology.
direction: Non-greedy population basin-hopping with contact-graph diversity: maintain a pool of 12–20 LP-polished local optima, initialized from the record plus strongly perturbed/rebuilt variants, and accept worse candidates with Metropolis probability $\exp(-(v-v_{\rm best})/T)$ for $T$ annealed from $2\times10^{-4}$ to $10^{-6}$ over the time budget instead of always restarting from the incumbent. Measure diversity by contact-graph Hamming distance (contacts at slack $<10^{-7}$) and forbid replacing a pool member by a candidate whose graph is within, say, 20 edges of an existing member unless it beats that member. Add recombination: align two parents by an orthogonal Procrustes transform (SVD of $X^\top Y$ in $\mathbb R^5$), match points with `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` on Euclidean distance, take matched points from one parent and unmatched regions from the other, renormalize, anneal briefly, and LP-polish—this preserves large well-packed patches from two basins while creating new contacts at the seams.

Delete a BFS contact-graph cluster of 20-50 points and globally rebuild it by greedy farthest-point sampling plus annealed softmax repulsion and frozen/unfrozen LP polishing.
direction: Large-cluster delete-and-rebuild: instead of reinserting 2–6 points, repeatedly delete a connected cluster of 20–50 points obtained by BFS in the contact graph from a seed chosen among the rattler's nearest points or a degree-$\ge11$ point, freeze the remaining points, and rebuild the cluster globally: sample $\sim10^5$ random unit vectors, greedily select replacements maximizing the minimum angle first to the frozen set and then among themselves, optimize only the free points with annealed softmax repulsion ($\beta:50\to500$, tangent-projected) followed by LP polishing with frozen points held fixed, then unfreeze and fully LP-polish. Vary cluster size and seed on each trial and retain the best few distinct outcomes; this directly creates angular room and rewires dozens of contacts at once, which point-at-a-time void filling cannot do.

idea: Greedy basin-hopping that forces topology changes by overload-targeted cap removal and void re-insertion combined with annealed exponential repulsion smoothing and trust-region tangent LP polishing to achieve balanced load-sharing.

Excise 9–15-point contact neighbourhoods around overloaded or rattler-adjacent centres and rebuild them by sequential 50k-sample maximin void filling with frozen-background local repulsion before global annealed repulsion and LP polish.
direction: Perform contact-neighbourhood excision and patch reconstruction: choose either the 13-contact point, the rattler’s nearest jammed cluster, or a random point with at least nine contacts, delete that point together with 8–14 of its contact neighbours, freeze the remaining points, and rebuild the deleted patch sequentially by sampling 50,000 random sphere directions, greedily choosing maximin void directions against both frozen and already-reinserted points, locally repelling the patch points, and only afterwards unfreezing all 173 points for annealed repulsion followed by LP polishing; cycle through several non-overlapping neighbourhoods rather than shaking the whole configuration.

idea: Freeze the zero-contact rattler and push the other 172 points away from it with a tangent LP minimizing its maximum, then unfreeze and re-polish with its nearest pairs forced into the active set to obtain a balanced code.
direction: Force the rattler into the active set with a targeted feasibility search: identify the zero-contact point $r$, freeze its direction initially, and repeatedly solve the tangent LP/smooth hinge problem for the other 172 points with pairs not involving $r$ constrained to at most the current record value but pairs involving $r$ constrained to at most record$-\varepsilon$, cycling $\varepsilon\in\{10^{-4},3\times10^{-4},10^{-3},3\times10^{-3}\}$; then unfreeze $r$, include its nearest 15 pairs plus all pairs within $5\times10^{-3}$ of the maximum, and run the usual LP polish, accepting the result whenever the rattler acquires at least three contacts even if the intermediate maximum is temporarily worse.

idea: Escape the jammed 172-point core by alternating void-based re-insertion of overloaded plus rattler points, cap restarts and fresh Riesz-energy continuations with Procrustes-plus-assignment recombination, each followed by trust-region tangent LP polishing to land in a new balanced basin.
Freeze the zero-contact rattler and force it into the active set by minimizing its maximum cosine under a record cap for all other pairs, then unfreeze with r-focused LP polish.

idea: Balanced-load annealing with void re-insertion and trust-region LP polishing to escape the rattler basin
Below-record target continuation with softplus violation and Riemannian Adam to force basin changes toward unattainable targets.
direction: Use below-record target continuation that permits uphill exploration: set targets $T=0.757,0.754,0.751,0.748$ in succession and minimize a smooth violation objective such as $\sum_{i<j}\operatorname{softplus}(\alpha(c_{ij}-T))/\alpha$ with $\alpha$ increasing from 200 to 3000, using Riemannian Adam or L-BFGS on the sphere from the record, strongly perturbed record copies, and independent random starts; retain trajectories according to total violation and number of pairs above $T$, not merely the current maximum, and apply the LP polish only to trajectories whose count of near-maximal pairs changes substantially or whose violation falls below a preset threshold.

De novo algebraic/lattice pool greedy maximin with Riesz-softmax continuation and LP polish over diverse basins
direction: De novo structured constructions from algebraic/lattice candidate pools, ignoring the record except as fallback: build a large pool of unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^5$ from coordinate patterns such as permutations/signs of $(1,1,0,0,0)/\sqrt2$, $(1,1,1,1,0)/2$, $(1,0,0,0,0)$, $D_5$-type vectors, cyclic orbits $(1,\cos\theta,\cos2\theta,\ldots)$-style Fourier vectors, and random spherical-design points, then greedily select 173 points by maximin cosine, run Riesz/softmax continuation with exponent/temperature scheduled from soft to hard (e.g. effective $\alpha=5\to200$), and LP polish. Maintain several structurally different seeds and select by final max cosine and contact-graph signature, not by distance to the record, so the search can discover a basin whose contact topology is not inherited from the published configuration.

idea: Homotopy across N with void-insertion growth, overload deletion from N+1/N+2, and Procrustes+Hungarian recombination of diverse local optima.
direction: Build a diverse population through particle-number homotopy and recombination: first optimize codes for $N=168$–172 from multiple random seeds, insert additional points one at a time into the largest spherical voids found from 20,000 candidate directions with repulsion-plus-LP after each insertion up to $N=173$, and also optimize $N=174$ or 175 and delete the most overloaded point before repolishing; maintain an archive distinguished by contact-graph pattern and minimum contact count, then recombine distinct local optima after orthogonal Procrustes alignment and Hungarian point matching by taking complementary subsets, repairing the merged code by void insertion, annealing, and final LP polishing.

idea: Rattler-centred frozen excision with greedy void reinsertion and block LSE refinement then global polish.
direction: Rattler-centred frozen-environment excision with exact reinsertion: identify the rattler and remove it together with $k=4,8,$ or $12$ points chosen from its nearest neighbours in cosine and from the highest-contact points, freeze the other $173-k$ points, and solve only the $4k$-dimensional problem of placing the removed points to minimise their maximum cosine to the frozen set and each other, using $20{,}000$ random sphere samples plus greedy void filling followed by `scipy.optimize` SLSQP/log-sum-exp refinement on the removed block alone. Only after this frozen optimum is below or near $0.75856$ should all points be unfrozen for a short smooth anneal and final LP polish; enumerate several removal sets systematically within about 120 seconds, guard every stage with try/except and time checks, and return the loaded record if no candidate beats it, avoiding the crashes of earlier unconstrained rebuild attempts.

idea: Coherent orbit/community kicks on the contact graph with tabu cycling plus softmax repel and trust-region LP polish to escape the symmetry-locked basin.
direction: Coherent orbit/cluster kicks that preserve-or-break symmetry as a unit: compute the contact graph at threshold $10^{-9}$, hash each point by its sorted contact-cosines and contact-neighbour degrees to propose approximate equivalence classes/orbits, and also find communities by greedy modularity on the contact graph; then, instead of kicking individual points, apply a random small rotation in a random 2-plane of $\mathbb{R}^5$ to one whole orbit/community, or move it along a random tangent field constant on the class, with amplitudes $0.02$--$0.15$, before LP polishing. Cycle over classes and over preserve-one-class/break-one-class moves, keep a tabu list of tried classes, always retain the unmodified record as fallback, and use the remaining time budget for LP polish of the best perturbed candidate; this directly attacks the symmetry-locked topology rather than immediately destroying and then recreating it.

idea: Escape the over-jammed symmetric basin by load-balancing the rattler with coherent topology surgeries — overload-to-void transplants, rigid cap rotations and subset orthogonal remixing — diversified over a small pool with Riesz plus soft-max annealing before trust-region LP polishing.

Escape the over-jammed symmetric basin by large overload-to-void topology moves that delete whole caps of high-contact points and greedily reinsert them into maximin voids to force the rattler load-bearing, followed by soft-to-hard annealed repulsion and trust-region LP polishing from a diverse archive.
Replace overloaded points by maximin voids and re-polish to jump basins instead of LP-relaxing the same jam.
